items.question: How does MLlib's KernelDensity combine Gaussian kernels around each observation to produce its density estimate?
items.answer: It averages the PDFs of normal distributions centered on each sample.
items.quote:
It achieves
this estimate by expressing the PDF of the empirical distribution at a particular point as the
mean of PDFs of normal distributions centered around each of the samples.
items.note: Kernel density estimation appears only in docs/mllib-statistics.md in the corpus.
items.review_note: Quote is an exact substring (checked with python, occurs once); it states the answer; longest shared run is 2 words; grep finds KDE/KernelDensity only in mllib-statistics.

items.question: By default, how long can an unused Kafka consumer stay pooled on an executor before Structured Streaming may evict it?
items.answer: 5 minutes, set by spark.kafka.consumer.cache.timeout.
items.quote: spark.kafka.consumer.cache.timeout | 5m (5 minutes) | The minimum amount of time a consumer may sit idle in the pool before it is eligible for eviction by the evictor. | 3.0.0
items.note: I used this row instead of cache.capacity=64 and the caching key, because docs/streaming-kafka-0-10-integration.md describes both of those for DStreams (default size 64, keyed by topicpartition and group.id). The fetchedData timeout row in the same section is also 5m, but it is about a different pool.
items.review_note: Exact substring, once; the question names the consumer pool, so the 5m fetchedData row is not a second answer; the DStream Kafka doc gives capacity, enable flag and key but no timeout; no leakage.

items.answer: As the weighted average of all labels for that feature.

items.question: What type rule must the THEN and ELSE results of a Spark SQL CASE expression satisfy?
items.answer: They must be the same type or coercible to a common type.
items.quote: Specifies the then expression based on the `boolean_expression` condition; `then_expression` and `else_expression` should all be same type or coercible to a common type.
items.note: sql-ref-ansi-compliance.md (Least Common Type Resolution) says this indirectly: least common type resolution is used to 'Derive the result type for expressions such as the case expression'. The same sentence also appears under else_expression; the quote is the then_expression sentence, which occurs once.
items.review_note: Exact substring, once; 'coercible'/'common type' appear elsewhere only in ansi-compliance's least-common-type text (line 216 names the case expression), so also_in is right; no leakage.

items.question: If a session variable created with DECLARE VARIABLE has the same name as a column, which one does an unqualified reference pick?
items.answer: The column; the variable is used only if no column or alias matches, unless qualified with session/system.session.
items.quote:
Unless you qualify a variable with `session` or `system.session`, a variable is only resolved after
Spark fails to resolve a name to a column or column alias.
items.note: drop-variable.md mentions only the system.session qualifier. The name-resolution order is described only here.
items.review_note: Exact substring, once; grep finds the resolution order only here (drop-variable, set-var and identifier docs do not state it); answer is 17 words; not yes/no; no leakage.

items.question: How is the lift of an association rule calculated by spark.ml's FPGrowthModel?
items.answer: support(antecedent U consequent) divided by support(antecedent) x support(consequent).
items.quote: `lift: double`: A measure of how well the antecedent predicts the consequent, calculated as `support(antecedent U consequent) / (support(antecedent) x support(consequent))`
items.note: ml-migration-guide.md mentions lift but does not give the formula. mllib-frequent-pattern-mining.md does not cover lift.
items.review_note: Exact substring, once; the only other 'lift' hit is 'restriction is lifted' (Imputer) in ml-migration-guide, so the note's claim that it mentions lift is wrong but the item stands; no leakage.
